session_1.title: Session 1 of 7 — What is Etiology?
session_1.scenario: Two calves are born on the same farm, live in the exact same pasture, and drink the same water. After a sudden drop in temperature, one calf develops a severe cough and fever, while the other stays healthy and active.
session_1.question: Why do you think one calf got sick while the other stayed healthy?
options: A) The sick calf was just unlucky.
B) Something specific happened to or entered the sick calf that didn't affect the healthy one.
C) Calves always take turns getting sick.
session_1.feedback_correct: Correct! Disease occurs because a specific cause acts upon an animal.

term_card.meaning: The study of the cause or origin of disease.
term_card.example: Determining whether a cow's respiratory signs are caused by a virus, bacteria, or cold stress.

session_1.recap: Etiology asks the central question: WHY did this animal become sick?

session_2.title: Session 2 of 7 — Predisposing Causes
session_2.scenario: A herd of mixed-breed cattle is exposed to intense sunlight. White-faced Hereford cattle develop skin lesions on their unpigmented eyelids, while fully pigmented Angus cattle show no lesions.
session_2.question: What type of factor made the Hereford cattle more susceptible?
session_2.feedback_correct: Spot on! Lack of skin pigmentation is a predisposing factor that increases susceptibility to UV damage.

term_card.meaning: A factor intrinsic or extrinsic to the animal that increases its susceptibility to disease.
term_card.example: Age, species, breed, sex, or lack of pigmentation.

session_2.recap: Predisposing causes do not directly initiate disease; they make the animal more vulnerable.

session_3.title: Session 3 of 7 — Physical Causes
session_3.scenario: A dog is brought to the clinic with severe tissue damage and limb fractures following a motor vehicle accident.
session_3.question: Which category of direct cause initiated this condition?
session_3.feedback_correct: Correct! Mechanical kinetic energy (trauma) directly caused the structural damage.

term_card.meaning: Environmental energy or force acting on tissues (Trauma, Heat, Cold, Radiation).
term_card.example: Frostbite from extreme cold or burns from excess heat.

session_3.recap: Physical causes involve external physical forces or thermal radiation damaging body tissues.

session_4.title: Session 4 of 7 — Chemical Causes and Toxins
session_4.scenario: A farm dog accidentally ingests a stored pesticide container and shows severe muscular twitching and salivation.
session_4.question: How should this cause be classified?
session_4.feedback_correct: Correct! Pesticides are chemical toxins that disrupt physiological function.

term_card.meaning: Substances (acids, alkalis, plant toxins, pesticides) that alter cell function chemically.

session_4.recap: Chemicals and toxins act through chemical injury rather than mechanical force.

session_5.title: Session 5 of 7 — Biological / Viable Causes
session_5.scenario: A flock of sheep exhibits severe anemia and bottle jaw due to a heavy Haemonchus parasite infection in the abomasum.
session_5.question: What broad etiological group does Haemonchus belong to?
session_5.feedback_correct: Correct! Helminths and parasites are living (viable) biological causes of disease.

term_card.meaning: Living infectious organisms including bacteria, viruses, fungi, mycoplasma, rickettsia, and parasites.
term_card.example: Foot-and-Mouth Disease virus in cattle or Anthrax bacteria in sheep.

session_5.recap: Biological causes are living or replicating agents that invade or parasitize host tissues.

session_6.title: Session 6 of 7 — Nutritional, Immunological & Miscellaneous
session_6.scenario: A high-producing dairy cow collapses shortly after calving due to acute blood calcium depletion (milk fever).
session_6.question: What type of cause is milk fever?
session_6.feedback_correct: Exactly right! Acute metabolic deficiency of calcium around parturition causes milk fever.

term_card.meaning: Disease resulting from acute or chronic deficiency or excess of essential nutrients.
term_card.example: Vitamin B1 deficiency causing neurological signs in poultry.

session_6.recap: Nutritional, immunological (hypersensitivity), iatrogenic (treatment-related), and idiopathic causes complete our definitive list.

session_7.title: Session 7 of 7 — Complete Classification & Consolidation
session_7.scenario: A dog develops a severe allergic reaction (anaphylaxis) minutes after receiving an insect sting.
session_7.question: Which etiological category applies here?
session_7.feedback_correct: Excellent! Anaphylaxis is an extreme, rapid immunological hypersensitivity reaction.

term_card.meaning: Complete organization of disease causes into Predisposition and Definitive factors.
term_card.example: Refer to the summary matrix below.

session_7.recap: You have completed all 7 micro-sessions in Etiology!
